This page installs SCGSim and the public component library used by the
tutorials. Installing SCGSim does not install Palace or AEDT; you set those up
separately on the computer that runs the solver.

::: {.callout-note title="Before you start"}
- Python 3.12 or 3.13.
- Git.
- For AEDT workflows: a Windows or Linux computer with AEDT 2024.2 and a
  licence.
:::

## Step 1: Get the source

Clone SCGSim and create a fresh virtual environment:

```bash
git clone --branch main https://github.com/OrPenStrike/scgsim.git
cd scgsim
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
```

The `main` branch is the latest stable release. If you are reading the docs
for a specific version, use the version selector at the top of the site and
check out the matching tag instead.

## Step 2: Install SCGSim

Install SCGSim with the extras for the work you do on this computer:

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[palace]'
```

::: {.table-responsive}

| Extra | Use it to | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| *(none)* `.` | Read returned results and show reports | NumPy, Plotly |
| `palace` | Prepare Palace runs | GDSFactory 9.x, GDS reader, Gmsh |
| `aedt` | Prepare HFSS, Q3D or Q2D runs | GDS reader, PyAEDT 1.3.0 |
| `aedt-epr` | Prepare HFSS runs with surface EPR from a component | `aedt` plus GDSFactory 9.x and KLayout 0.30.x |
| `visualization` | Render 3D previews of the prepared geometry | Mesh reader, image tools, PyVista |

:::

Combine extras with commas, for example `'.[palace,visualization]'`. Geometry
previews need a working OpenGL or EGL context; see
[Geometry preview](../geometry-preview.qmd) for headless options.

## Step 3: Install the tutorial components

The tutorials use components from the OrPen SC PDK. Install it into the same
environment so that SCGSim and the PDK resolve the same GDSFactory and KLayout
versions. This command installs everything the beginner tutorials need, for
both Palace and AEDT, plus a Jupyter kernel:

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[palace,aedt-epr,visualization]' 'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orcapen-sc-pdk.git@51985d9507025e8241205712e866c0b804de29b9' ipykernel
```

Some larger examples need a different PDK revision. Their environments are
listed in [Environments for other examples](#example-environments).

## Step 4: Check the installation

```python
from importlib.metadata import version
print(version("scgsim"))
```

Note this version, and the PDK revision, with your study. Results depend on
both.

## Step 5: Set up the solver host

You can prepare runs on one computer and run the solver on another. The
solver host needs:

- **Palace:** a `palace` executable, or a wrapper script that starts it with
  MPI. If your cluster uses environment modules, note the `module load`
  command; you pass it to SCGSim when preparing a run. See the
  [Palace installation guide](https://awslabs.github.io/palace/stable/install/).
- **AEDT:** AEDT 2024.2, a licence, and PyAEDT 1.3.0 in the Python environment
  that runs the generated script. The script starts AEDT, saves the project
  and closes AEDT when it finishes.

Reading returned results needs only SCGSim; it does not need Palace or AEDT.

## Environments for other examples {#example-environments}

These examples use a different PDK revision from the tutorials. Give each its
own virtual environment, created as in Step 1, and install with the command
below instead of Step 3.

### Circular Pad {#env-circular-pad}

Used by the [Circular Pad LC study](palace-eigenmode.qmd#circular-pad-lc-study).
Needs SCGSim 1.1.0rc1 or later:

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[palace,visualization]' 'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orcapen-sc-pdk.git@ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52' ipykernel
```

### Flip-chip Xmon {#env-xmon}

Used by the [flip-chip Xmon example](../tutorial-xmon-input.qmd). Replace
`palace` with the extra for your backend:

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[palace]' 'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orcapen-sc-pdk.git@35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9'
```
